title: Performance of DeepSeek-R1 in Ophthalmology: An Evaluation of Clinical Decision-Making and Cost-Effectiveness

paper.authors: Mikhail, Farah, Milad, Nassrallah, Mihalache, Milad, Antaki, Balas, Popovic, Feo, Muni, Keane, Duval
paper.venue_note: medRxiv preprint (posted 2025-02-12, CC-BY-ND 4.0), not peer reviewed; 'Supplemental Material: None'
paper.repo_note: The scaffold candidate github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-k1.5 is reference 41 (third-party), not an artifact of this paper

dependence.note: The claim is the accuracy of two LLMs on 300 case MCQs and their equivalence (McNemar) - entirely model output; cost analysis derives from token counts of the same outputs.

claim.statement: OpenAI o1 (o1-2024-12-17 via API, temperature 0.3, Plan-and-Solve+ zero-shot prompt) answered 246/300 (82.0%; 95% CI 77.3-85.9) StatPearls ophthalmology case MCQs correctly - identical to DeepSeek-R1 (246/300; McNemar p=1.000), with moderate inter-model agreement (kappa=0.503, p<0.001) and no significant subspecialty differences (Table 1, Table 2, Table 3).
claim.metric: proportion of 300 single-best-answer MCQs correct (one response per case); Wilson 95% CI; McNemar test on paired outcomes; Cohen's kappa
claim.original_source: Table 1 (accuracy by subspecialty with 95% CI and p), Table 2 (2x2 contingency), Table 3 (kappa); Results text; Cost-Effectiveness section

protocol.model_note: Named explicitly in the cost analysis ('OpenAI's o1-2024-12-17 model'); accessed via API with 'automated mass prompting techniques via Google Sheets'
protocol.prompt_source: not available - paper describes the Zero-Shot Plan-and-Solve+ (PS+) prompt (Wang et al. 2023) applied to the full case description + MCQ + four options, without quoting the wording; ref 24 (authors' previous study) may contain it

params.temperature: 0.3 as reported - NOTE: the o1 API does not accept temperature values other than the default (1), so the reported setting cannot have been applied as described
params.other: text-only prompts (images removed from the 21 cases that had them); DeepSeek-R1 comparator run through the public chat UI with default settings

protocol.evaluation: Automatic letter match against the StatPearls answer key (how the final letter was parsed from o1's free-form output is not described); McNemar (paired), Cohen's kappa, Wilson CIs in R 4.4.2

artifacts.data_note: 300 cases 'from an online database of publicly available questions from StatPearls' - the selected case list/IDs are not provided and StatPearls question content is proprietary
artifacts.notes: No supplementary material, no repository, no response logs.

blockers: 300 StatPearls case-MCQs: selection not shared ('Supplemental Material: None') and the content is copyrighted
exact PS+ prompt wording not given
reported temperature 0.3 is not settable for o1 via the API - the protocol as described is not exactly reproducible
DeepSeek-R1 comparator used the web chat UI (no version/parameter control) - equivalence half of the claim is not API-reproducible as run

budget.assumptions: 300 cases x 3 seeds; ~450 input tokens per case (322 avg case+MCQ per paper + PS+ prompt); 2,000 output tokens per item per the reasoning-model rule (paper's visible output was ~352 tokens/case but hidden reasoning tokens are billed). CONDITIONAL on obtaining the case list.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1: survival if o1-2024-12-17 accuracy has a Wilson 95% CI (n=300) overlapping 0.82 [0.773-0.859]; the equivalence claim (o1 = DeepSeek-R1, McNemar p>0.05) can only be judged if DeepSeek-R1 (open weights, API 'deepseek-reasoner') is re-run as the permanent axis - then direction = no significant difference.
judgment.notes: Subspecialty CIs are very wide (n=10-69); judge only the overall accuracy.

user_checks: Request the 300-case StatPearls list (IDs/titles) and the exact PS+ prompt from the corresponding author (renaud.duval@gmail.com)? Without it the card cannot run.
If obtained: is the core claim 'o1 = 82.0%' (capability_level, o1 only) or 'o1 equals DeepSeek-R1' (requires re-running R1 via API, which differs from the paper's chat-UI run)?
Accept running o1 at the API default temperature (the paper's 0.3 cannot be applied)?
domain_notes: Cases are StatPearls board-style ophthalmology vignettes classified into 10 AAO BCSC subspecialties (Retina/Vitreous n=69 largest, Cataract n=10 smallest); the authors acknowledge probable training-data leakage from StatPearls. The cost analysis excluded chain-of-thought tokens for both models, so the 15x cost ratio is an underestimate of true billed cost. The preprint is not peer reviewed.
